main.title: Earth Day
main.summary: The first Earth Day took place on 22 April 1970 as an American mobilisation for environmental protection.

cards.heading: Earth Day
cards.text: The first Earth Day took place on 22 April 1970 as an American mobilisation for environmental protection. Senator Gaylord Nelson proposed a nationwide teach-in and recruited activist Denis Hayes to coordinate it. The idea grew beyond an educational gathering into events across the country, with the name supplied by advertising writer Julian Koenig. A separate proposal by peace activist John McConnell had marked the spring equinox. The April observance developed into an annual international occasion, bringing environmental questions into public meetings, education and collective action.

main.title: Intel 1103
main.summary: The Intel 1103 is a dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) integrated circuit (IC) developed and fabricated by Intel.

cards.heading: Intel 1103
cards.text: The Intel 1103 is a dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) integrated circuit (IC) developed and fabricated by Intel. Introduced in October 1970, the 1103 was the first commercially available DRAM IC; and due to its small physical size and low price relative to magnetic-core memory, it replaced the latter in many applications. When it was introduced in 1970, initial production yields were poor, and it was not until the fifth stepping of the production masks that it became available in large quantities during 1971. Intel shipped the 250,000th 1103 RAM chip in June 1974.

main.title: Floppy disk
main.summary: IBM introduced the first floppy disks in 1971, using an eight-inch flexible magnetic surface to store digital data.

cards.heading: Floppy disk
cards.text: IBM introduced the first floppy disks in 1971, using an eight-inch flexible magnetic surface to store digital data. A drive read or wrote the disk while it turned inside a protective cover. Smaller formats followed: first the five-and-a-quarter-inch disk, then the more compact three-and-a-half-inch version. For computer users, a program or document became something that could be carried to another machine. Drives of different sizes sometimes shared a PC before the smaller format became dominant in the 1990s. The disk's changing dimensions accompanied its growing role in everyday software distribution and file exchange.

main.title: Intel 4004
main.summary: The Intel 4004, released by the Intel Corporation on November 15, 1971, was the first in a long line of Intel central processing units (CPUs).

cards.heading: Intel 4004
cards.text:
The Intel 4004, released by the Intel Corporation on November 15, 1971, was the first in a long line of Intel central processing units (CPUs). Priced at US$60 (equivalent to $477 in 2025), the chip marked both a technological and economic milestone in computing.

The 4-bit 4004 CPU was the first significant commercial example of large-scale integration, using the abilities of the MOS silicon gate technology (SGT) to integrate the CPU into a single chip. Compared to the existing technology, SGT enabled twice the transistor density and five times the operating speed, making future single-chip CPUs feasible. The MCS-4 chipset design, of which the 4004 was a part, served as a model on how to use SGT for complex logic and memory circuits, accelerating the adoption of SGT by the world's semiconductor industry.

main.title: Munich 1972 Olympic Games
main.summary: Munich hosted the Games of the XX Olympiad from 26 August to 11 September 1972.

cards.heading: Munich 1972 Olympic Games
cards.text: Munich hosted the Games of the XX Olympiad from 26 August to 11 September 1972. West Germany sought a democratic, optimistic image after Berlin's 1936 Games, expressed in the motto the cheerful Games. Otl Aicher's visual identity used a blue sun emblem, sky-blue clothing and the dachshund mascot Waldi. The event was overshadowed by the Munich massacre: members of the Palestinian group Black September attacked the Israeli delegation, and eleven of its members were killed. The attack profoundly changed the meaning of an edition conceived as an international celebration.

main.title: C
main.summary: Dennis Ritchie created C at Bell Labs in 1972, developing it from the earlier B language.

cards.heading: C
cards.text: Dennis Ritchie created C at Bell Labs in 1972, developing it from the earlier B language. It first supported utilities for Unix and then the rewriting of the operating system's kernel. C gave programmers relatively direct access to a machine's architecture while providing a language that could be implemented across different systems. Its use spread during the 1980s, from operating systems and drivers to applications and embedded devices. The C Programming Language, co-written by Ritchie, became a practical reference for programmers learning how to express that control in portable source code.

main.title: The Godfather
main.summary: The Godfather follows the Corleone family as Michael moves from its margins towards command of its criminal business.

cards.heading: The Godfather
cards.text: The Godfather follows the Corleone family as Michael moves from its margins towards command of its criminal business. Francis Ford Coppola directed the 1972 film and adapted Mario Puzo's novel with its author. Marlon Brando plays Vito Corleone and Al Pacino his youngest son, whose changing position gives the family story its central movement. Filming in New York and Sicily placed domestic rooms and public streets around their dealings. Nino Rota's music, with additional pieces by Carmine Coppola, gives those loyalties and ceremonies a recurring sound.

main.title: Watergate scandal
main.summary: On 17 June 1972, operatives linked to Richard Nixon's re-election campaign were caught breaking into Democratic Party headquarters at the Watergate complex in Washington.

cards.heading: Watergate scandal
cards.text: On 17 June 1972, operatives linked to Richard Nixon's re-election campaign were caught breaking into Democratic Party headquarters at the Watergate complex in Washington. The investigation grew from a burglary into an examination of political spying and White House obstruction. Reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein helped expose the connections, guided by their confidential source Deep Throat. The administration destroyed evidence and interfered with investigators as it tried to conceal its involvement. Revelations after the burglars' trial led to Senate scrutiny and an impeachment process. Nixon resigned in August 1974.

main.title: Oil crisis
main.summary: In October 1973, Arab oil exporters imposed an embargo on countries they regarded as supporting Israel during the Yom Kippur War.

cards.heading: Oil crisis
cards.text: In October 1973, Arab oil exporters imposed an embargo on countries they regarded as supporting Israel during the Yom Kippur War. Saudi Arabia led the effort, and the targets included the United States, Japan and several European countries. The restriction turned a regional conflict into an international energy shock. By the time the embargo ended in March 1974, the world oil price had risen from about three dollars a barrel to nearly twelve. The sharp increase affected economies and political decisions well beyond the countries directly involved in the war.

main.title: Amarcord
main.subtitle: A year in a town remembered through its people
main.summary: Amarcord returns to the provincial world of Federico Fellini's youth through an ensemble of families, schoolchildren and local celebrities. Written with Tonino Guerra and released in 1973, the film follows the adolescent Titta through the seasons of a town in 1930s Italy. Personal memories take shape inside public rituals, Catholic education and Fascist displays.

cards.heading: A town and its seasons
cards.text: Amarcord returns to the provincial world of Federico Fellini's youth through an ensemble of families, schoolchildren and local celebrities. Written with Tonino Guerra and released in 1973, the film follows the adolescent Titta through the seasons of a town in 1930s Italy. Personal memories take shape inside public rituals, Catholic education and Fascist displays.

cards.heading: The people who fill a memory
cards.text: The town comes alive through recurring encounters. School lessons become contests between teachers and pupils; family meals turn into quarrels; the inhabitants gather for celebrations, gossip and extraordinary sights. Titta's household gives these episodes a familiar centre, while figures such as Gradisca seem larger than the streets around them. The changing seasons supply continuity without forcing every incident into a single plot. A memory may be funny, embarrassing or tender, and the film allows those feelings to sit together.

cards.heading: Affection and authority
cards.text: The affectionate recollections also contain coercion and cruelty. Titta's father encounters the violence of the Fascist authorities, placing political power inside the family's experience. Elsewhere, collective excitement makes the town look at itself as a spectacle. Giuseppe Rotunno's colour photography and Nino Rota's recurring music help connect these different registers. The result gives childhood a recognisable emotional texture while leaving room for the exaggerations, omissions and performances through which people tell stories about where they came from.
